findings.title: OR SQL fragments are unsafe to AND with more predicates
findings.body: Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of a team-booking predicate and a personal-booking predicate, joined as `(${left}) OR (${right})` in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition. That groups each side only; it does not parenthesize the whole OR. When eventTypeId and memberUserId are absent, getBaseConditions returns that fragment unchanged. SQL binds AND tighter than OR, so a caller query `WHERE ${conditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` is parsed as team-booking-predicate OR (personal-booking-predicate AND startTime >= from). Every team booking for an authorized team is included even when it fails the date range or any other AND predicate the caller adds. The event-type filter has the same shape, `("eventTypeId" = id) OR ("eventParentId" = id)`, with no outer parentheses. Interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${eventTypeFilter}` is parsed as (auth AND eventTypeId = id) OR (eventParentId = id), so any booking whose parent event type matches is returned even if authorization fails. getBaseConditions does wrap both sides when a filter is present, but the no-filter return value and the public getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions fragments are not embed-safe. The old Prisma where-objects were grouped by the query engine, so this is a regression of the raw-SQL conversion. Wrap every fragment in an outer pair of parentheses before returning it.

findings.title: Prisma.sql toEqual checks do not match nested fragments
findings.body: The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 expect a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. The service builds those conditions with Array.reduce, nesting Prisma.sql fragments, and Prisma.sql does not flatten nested fragments until execution. The actual object has inner Sql values; the expected object has raw ids and arrays in values. Deep equality fails even when the SQL text and parameters match, so these tests fail in CI and do not validate authorization or filter SQL. Compare a flattened statement and parameter list, or execute the SQL.

findings.title: Team and org authorization SQL is never executed
findings.body: The only database query in this file is the user-scope getBaseConditions case, which is userId equality AND teamId IS NULL. Team and org authorization, including teamId/userId = ANY(array) and the isTeamBooking OR groups, are only compared as objects. PostgreSQL array binding for Prisma raw parameters and AND/OR precedence are therefore untested. Execute those fragments with $queryRaw against rows that must be included and rows that must be excluded (another org's team, a non-member personal booking, a team booking versus a personal booking, and an extra AND predicate such as a date range).
